name: ABAW2 / Aff-Wild2 benchmark
description: The Affective Behavior Analysis in-the-wild (ABAW2) 2021 Competition is the second -- following the first very successful ABAW Competition held in conjunction with IEEE FG 2020- Competition that aims at automatically analyzing affect. ABAW2 is split into three Challenges, each one addressing one of the three main behavior tasks of valence-arousal estimation, basic expression classification and action unit detection. All three Challenges are based on a common benchmark database, Aff-Wild2, which is a large scale in-the-wild database and the first one to be annotated for all these three tasks. In this paper, we describe this Competition, to be held in conjunction with ICCV 2021. We present the three Challenges, with the utilized Competition corpora. We outline the evaluation metrics and present the baseline system with its results. More information regarding the Competition is provided in the Competition site: https://ibug.doc.ic.ac.uk/resources/iccv-2021-2nd-abaw.
evaluation_method: Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) for valence-arousal; F1-score / F1-macro (and related classification metrics) for expression classification and action unit detection
general_score_metric: CCC (primary for valence-arousal) and F1 / F1-macro (primary for expressions and AUs)
reputation: Well-known and widely used benchmark in the affective computing / facial behavior analysis community for in-the-wild multi-task evaluation.
notes: Large in-the-wild dataset with multi-task annotations; class imbalance and annotation noise present; evaluation metrics differ by task so cross-task comparison requires care; non-LLM vision benchmark.
